analysis: Only documentation changed in the supplied units; no code was provided. provider-trust.md (head lines 79-86) changes invariant 4 from "Build publication is not qualification" (durable approval by an independently authenticated operator, CI keys cannot approve) to "Official registration is not runtime authorization". Under the new text, trusted CI registers the full official identity via the scoped release API, and manual approval and per-release hardware qualification are not required. Serving still needs Apple proof and receipt, matching code/runtime hashes, and nonrevoked status. docs/consumer/verification.md (head lines 14-18) adds a consistent statement for consumers. This shifts the trust root for A-017/T-054/TB-011 to the CI/release API, which the scope lists as out of scope (GitHub Actions/R2). The canonical threat model and the TB-011 limitation about operator signed-artifact qualification are now stale. Residual contradictions remain in provider-trust.md line 109 and verification.md line 13. The doc also warns that the platform persistence change must be deployed first, an ordering hazard. The next pass should check the actual code (release API scope, build_qualifications.go, the revocation tombstone path, the compatibility mappings) to confirm that durable rows are still checked at the final handoff and that revocation overrides CI registration. That code was not supplied, so this is a coverage limit.

findings.detail: The base text of provider-trust.md invariant 4 says serving requires an approved artifact/code identity ("Build publication is not qualification"). The base canonical context says an independently authenticated operator approves the exact signed binary and full CodeDirectory, and that CI release keys cannot grant approval. The head text replaces this with "Trusted CI registers the complete official identity through the existing scoped release API". It also says that "CI and repository writers are trusted for official build identity" and that "per-release hardware qualification and manual approval are not required". A compromised CI pipeline or release key could therefore register a malicious build and obtain App Attest serving authorization, with no human approval and no physical-Mac check. The provider would then receive plaintext consumer prompts. The threat model still lists GitHub Actions/R2 as out of scope, and T-054, A-017 and TB-011 still assert approval independent of CI. The head text also says the platform persistence change must be deployed before the provider workflow is used. Running them out of order could register or reject builds inconsistently. Fix: update A-017, T-054, TB-011 and the scope list to cover the CI-to-release-API trust path and the missing approval gate. Add compensating controls such as a scoped, rotatable CI key, an audit log, rapid revocation, and an alert on new identities. Alternatively, keep the operator approval requirement.
findings.title: Docs drop the independent operator-approval gate for App Attest builds; threat model not updated
